7. The Gazette Notifications regarding the acquisition of the lands recorded in plot Nos. 15, 31, 36, 41, 57, 69, 84, 117 and 17 of Mouza Chakuli are the subject matter of writ petition No.3210 of 2001. The notifications regarding the land recorded in CS and SA Plot Nos. 14, 43, 67, 73, 77 and 88 of the same Mouza are the subject matter of writ petition No. 7012 of 2003. The Notifications regarding the land recorded in CS and  SA Plot Nos. 73, 77, 57, 75, 68, 59, 61, 69, 71, 76 and 93 are the subject matter of writ petition No. 1973 of 2005, The Notifications regarding the land recorded in plot Nos. 85, 86, 87, 27, 33, 16, 65, 99, 81, 100, 62, 63, 66, 95, 97, 29, 94 and 98 are the subject matter of writ petition No. 4493 of 2005. 

 8. The petitioners, have challenged the alleged oral direction of the respondents to the petitioners to vacate the possession of the land described therein in Writ Petition No.7012 of 2003  But it appears to us from, the said petition that the petitioners substantially raised their grievance against the order of-acquisition of the land described therein. 

 9. The petitioners, in all the writ petitions, narrating their claim of title stated that the respondents did not comply the provisions of relevant law while milking requisition and subsequently acquisition of the land in question. No statutory notices under the provision of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (hereinafter referred as the Act) were served upon the petitioners or their predecessors-in-interest. It has also been stated that the questioned hinds were requisitioned by the Government in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 and those were subsequently derequisitioned during the pendency of writ petition Nos. 257 to 264, 302 to 311, 326, 327, 329, 339, 340, 343, 360, 370 to 374, 392 and 396 of 1969. The learned Deputy Attorney General for' the Government admitted in those writ petitions that, the lands in question were derequisitioned. Accordingly those rules were dis- charged as prayed for. It has further been stated that the petitioners have been possessing the disputed land. There are mosque, graveyard, temple, etc, in some plots. No compensation was paid to the petitioners on preparing the compensation assessment role. 

 11. The case of the Government, in substance, is that some portions of the lands in question were requisitioned and thereafter acquired by the Government by Gazette notification dated 19-1-1970. Government again requisitioned the said land and other questioned land for acquisition for Jatyo Rakkhi Bahini (including the land which were derequisitioned in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66) and finally acquired in LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 observing all the legal formalities. The notices under the provisions of the Act were served upon the owners and possessors of the said land. Compensation assessment rule was duly prepared and the owners received compensation. The decision of acquisition have been published in the official Gazette. The title and possession of the land in question had been vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. There was no illegality or irregularity in the process of acquisition. 

 13. Mr. JH Afric, the learned Advocate, at first, submits that the process of requisition and acquisition of the land in question in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 is a nullity in view of the fact that the same was not acquired for public purpose. The law did not authorize the respondents to acquire any land other than public purpose. He submits that, in fact, after making de requisition of the land in 1973, the Government left the process of acquisition in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66. The Government gave up their claim in the land after derequisition in 1973 by conduct. He further submits that the order of acquisition in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73, after making de requisition of the said land in 1973, is not permissible in law. He further submits that the original owners of the land including the petitioners had not received any statutory notice as per provisions of the Act. No compensation assessment role was prepared and award was not made in the name of the petitioners or their predecessors-in-interest. The respondents acquired some portion of some plots without any specification which is not permissible in law. He submits that while making such requisition and acquisition the respondents did not consider the hardship of the people who have been possessing the land since the day immemorial.. There are mosque, mandir, graveyard etc. in some portions of the plots. Government cannot take over possession of the said land. He finally submits that since the instant proceeding of requisition and acquisition has not been made in accordance with the provision of Law, the impugned Gazette Notifications are liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 14. Mr. SM Moonir the learned Advocate, drawing our attention to the provisions of sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Act, submits that the procedures as provided in those sections had not been complied. With while making requisition and acquisition of the land in question, He submits, that the said land had been derequisitioned in 1973, After admitting the story of derequisition, the Government is barred by the provision of estoppel to say that the same was not derequisitioned. He submits that from the order sheet of LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 it is apparent that no notice was served upon the owners of the land in question arid no compensation was assessed and paid to them. He submits that onus lies upon the Government to establish that the notice of requisition and acquisition were served duly upon the owners of the land. The proceeding of LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 and the impugned Gazette Notifications are liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 16. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General, submits that some portions of the land in question previously were acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 for housing scheme and accordingly Gazette Notification was published and after so notification the title and possession of the said land had been vested in the Government. Thereafter, the said land was handed over to Messrs Eastern Housing Ltd. The said portions of the land were again requisitioned for the public purpose in LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 and notice was issued upon the Eastern Housing Ltd. After due compliance of all legal formalities the said land was finally acquired. He submits that some portions of the land were requisitioned in LA Case No, 90 of 1965-66 but those were not acquired, Those lands were released from requisition. Thereafter, again requisitioned in LA Case No.5 of 197-2-73 and finally acquired. Rest of the lands were requisitioned and acquired in the said-LA Case afresh: Notices were duly served and compensation was duly assessed and paid. He submits that there is no illegality and irregularity in the process of requisition and subsequent acquisition. Finally he submits that the Government snail not remove any structure of mosque, mandir etc. and protect the same if it is detected that there are such institutions constructed either before or after acquisition of the questioned land, 

 18. It appears from the rule issuing order and prayer portion of the Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2001 that the petitioners have challenged the Gazette Notifications mentioned above in respect of the land of plot Nos. 15, 35, 36, 41, 57, 79, 84, 117, and 17. The petitioners have instituted the instant writ petition through their constituted power of attorneys, namely MA Awal and Sudhir Chandra Sharke On perusal of the power of attorney (Annexure-A) it appears 'that the petitioners did not execute power in respect of the land recorded in plot No. 57. In that view of the matter our considered opinion is that-the petition in respect of the land recorded in plot 'No. 57 does not deserve any consideration in connection with WP No, 3210 of 2001. Rest of the questioned lands are recorded ill plot Nos. 15, 35, 36, 41, 79, 84, 117 and 17, It appears from Annexure-B to the. Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2001 that the Government .decided to release some plots of different Mouzas from the order of requisition as requisitioned earlier in LA. Case No. 90 of 1965-66 with a view to make requisition and subsequent acquisition for, the scheme of Jatiyo Rakshi Bahini. The description of the land released from the order of requisition in LA Case No.90 of 1965-66 have been given in the schedule which shows that the land measuring an area of 64.1081 acres were released from the order of requisition from Mouza Digun and 0.77 acre of land of plot Nos. 62, 63, 64, 65 and 120 of Mouza Chakuli on 17-8-1973. On 24-8-1973, the land covering 14.70 acres were released from the, order of requisition from Digun Mouza. Thereafter, on 8-9- 1973 the land measuring an area of 27.7431 acres of different plots including plot Nos. 14, 17, 27, 33, 57, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 75, 77, 79, 85, 87, 95, 97 and 117 (questioned in these writ petitions) of Chakuli Mouza were released from requisition. It furthers appears that 130.7050 acres of land of Mouza Senpara Parbata, again 158.4481 acres of land of Mouza Senpara Parbata, 92.1684 acres of land of Baunia Mouza, 24.2717 acres of land of Mouza Digun, 12.96 acres of land of Mouza Merul, 1:42 acres of land of Mouza Senpara Parbata, 3 :03 acres on and of Mouza Chadogan and 49.1736 acres of land of Mouza Duaripara were released on different dates. That is, a total area of 290.3509 acres of land were released from the order of requisition. Out of those lands only 0.10 acre out of 0.40 acre of plot No. 17,0.77 acre of land out of 9.52 acres of plot No. 79,0.19 acre of land out. of 1.96 acres of plot No. 117) the subject matters of WP No.3210 of 2001) were released from, requisition as it appears from the order sheet of LA Case No.90 of 1965-66 produced by the writ petitioner of writ petition No. 3210 of 2001. It further appears from Arinexure-H (Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970) filed by the writ petitioners of WP No. 3210 of 2001 in their epoxy to the affidavit-in-opposition that some of the lands it question were acquired by the Government. The said Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 shows that those lands were requisitioned on 31st May, 1966. The entire lands of plot Nos. 15, 35, 36 and 41 and part of plot Nos. 57, 79, 84 and 117 were acquired by the said Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970. It has been submitted that the acquisition of land in the Case No. 90 of 1965-66 was not done for public purpose and legal process was not followed. it appears from the writ petitions that the petitioners did not challenge the legality and propriety of the process of requisition and acquisition in LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66. So it difficult for us to consider the submission of the 'learned Advocates in these petitions at this stage. 

 19. The learned Advocates, appearing for the petitioners in WP No. 3210 of 2010, submits that in fact, after releasing the land in question from requisition, the Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 became mere paper transaction. But on perusal of the order sheet of LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66 produced by the petitioners, (Annexure-B to the Writ Petition No.3210 of 2001) it appears that only' in respect of some portions of the land of disputed plot Nos.17,79 and 117 of WP No. 3210 of 2001 had been released from the order of requisition for the purpose" of acquiring the same for Jatya Rakshi Bahini, 'There' is nothing in Annexure-B that the entire land of the questioned plot Nos. 15,35,36,41 and part of the lands questioned of plot No. 57, 79, 84 and If 7 (except the land covering 0,77 acre out of 9.52 acres of plot No. 79,0.19 acre out of 1.96 acres of plot No. 117 and 0.10 acre out of plot No. 17) had been released from the requisition, 0.77 acres of land from plot No. 79, 0.19 acre from plot No. 117 and 0.10 acre of plot No.17 were released since those lands were not acquired by Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970. Rest is lands which are also subject matter of this writ petition that is, entire land of plots No. 15,35,36 and 41 and part of plot Nos. 79, 84, 17 and 117 were not released from requisition since those lands were finally acquired by Gazette Notification dated 19-7-1970. In absence of any material before us that after publication of the Gazette Notification" on 19-1-1970 (Annexure-H) regarding acquisition of the land of plot Nos. 15,35, 36 and 84 and the I? Art of plot Nos. 57, 79, 84, 117 and 17 the same had been released from acquisition it is difficult for us to accept the submission of the learned Advocate that the land acquired had been released from requisition .and acquisition. The Government is lawfully authorised to withdraw or release any land from the, acquisition before the payment of compensation and order of withdrawal or release must be published in the official Gazette but no such Gazette Notification has been produced before this Court, for consideration. After payment of compensation and publication regarding acquisitioning in official Gazette, the ‘title or the land be vested in the Movement free from and encumbrances and the law does not allow the Government to release the same at that stage. In the case of Bangladesh vs Commercial Trust of Bangladesh Ltd. 46 DLR (AD) 89 it has been held that after payment of compensation for acquisition of land no order can be made for derequisition of such acquired land. Similar view has been taken in the case of Sayed a Hossain vs Wega Fashion Sweater (Pvt) Limited 59 DLR (AD) 83 wherein it has been observed by their Lordships that there is no law authorising the Government to release any land once it .is vested in the Government by acquisition according to law. 

 20. It appears from the Writ Petition No. 7012 of 2003 that the petitioners of that writ petition, in fact, challenged the order of acquisition of land of plot Nos. 14, 43, 67,73,77 and 88 in the cover to protect their alleged possession stating that the respondents took an attempt to evict them serving oral notice by beating drum. The petitioners claimed 52 acre of land from plot Nos. 14 and 43, 0.43 acre of from plot No. 67, 0.06 acre from plot No. 73 (wherein it is claimed that there is a Mandir) 111 acres of land from plot No. 77 and 1.35 acres of land from plot Note 88. It appears from the Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 that the entire land of plot No. 43 and the part of the land of plot Nos. 67, 73, 77 and 88 were acquired by the Government. From Annexure-B to the writ petition No. 3210 of 2001 it appears that the rest. Lands, which were not acquired, of plot Nos. 14, 67, 77 had been released from the order of requisition, The said released land was subsequently requisitioned and finally acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 and notified in the official Gazette under section 5(7) of the Act. After so acquisition of the title of the petitioner had been extinguished and the same' was vested in the Government. 

 23. Now we shall consider the legality 'and propriety of the proceeding of LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73. It appears from the order dated: 1 0-11-1972 of LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 (Annexure-5 series to the Supplementary affidavit in opposition in WP No. 3210 of 2001) that the land of plot Nos. 15, 29, 35, 36, 41, 59, 61, 69, 71, 76, 81, 93, 94, 98, 99, 100 and part of the plot Nos. 14,57,63,65,67, 73, 77, 78, 79, 84 and 117 of Chakuli Mouza were requisitioned by the said order. From the Gazette Notification dated 19-1-1970 (Annexure-H to the affidavit in reply filed in W. 3210 of 2001) it appears that the lands of those plots were first requisitioned on 31st May 1966 and acquired by the said notification dated 19-1-1970. Thereby the title of those lands were vested in the Government: It is evident that requiring body was Messrs Eastern Housing Limited. From the orders of derequisition of LA Case No.5 of 1977-73 it appears that the land acquired and handed over to Messrs Eastern Housing Ltd had again been requisitioned for the purpose of acquisition. It was directed to publish the order of requisition in Tahshilders and village Panchayet's office of the locality and the contents of the order was to be published by beating of drum in the locality. It was argued by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the notice of the said order of requisition and subsequent acquisition had not been served upon the petitioners. Since the land as mentioned above had been acquired in 1970 by way of Gazette Notification and title of the same was vested to the Eastern Housing Ltd. through Government as per provision of section 5(7) of the Act, so service of notice to the petitioners for those portions of questioned land does not arise at all. It appears from page 133 of the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition filed in Writ Petition No. 3210 of 2001 that 'notice under section 3 of the Act was issued upon the Eastern Housing Ltd. in respect of the land of the plot as mentioned above and the some other plots and same was accepted on behalf of the Eastern Housing Ltd. It further appears from the order dated 11-11-1972 (page 17) that after assessment of the compensation the cheques were issued in favour of the Managing Director of Eastern Housing Ltd. Finally order of acquisition was published, in the impugned Gazette Notification dated 15-10-1974. From Annexure-D to the WP No. 3210 of 2001 it appears that the possession of the land as acquired was resumed by the Government by another impugned notification dated 13-11-1988. Annexure- D is the Notification regarding resumption of possession of the land acquired by notification dated 15-10-1974 but the petitioners of WP No. 3210 of 2001 have challenged the said notification terming the same as Notification regarding acquisition. 

 25.  From the order dated 10-9-1973 of LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 it appears that the, land of questioned plot Nos. 14, 17, 27, 33, 57, 62, 63, 65, 66,68, 75, 77, 79, 85, 87, 95, 97 and 117 of Mouza Chakuli were requisitioned. Similarly it was directed to publish notice to TahshiIders and village Panchayet's office and by beating drum in the locality: Nazir was directed to cause service of notice and to put up the service return. On, the same date notices under Section 5(1)(a) and 5(3) of Act were signed by Land Acquisition Officer and Nazir was again directed to cause service. It appears from the second order dated 10-9-1973 that the Kanongo assessed the compensation of a sum of Taka 48, 24, 272.52. Accordingly, after so assessment notice under sections 5(1)(a) and 5(3) of the Act were issued. It appears from the subsequent orders that one Wazedul Islam claiming himself the power of attorney of the persons against whom the compensation was awarded made an attempt to get the compensation but the authority concerned directed the office to verify the genuineness of such claim and after verification of the said power of attorney the said amount was paid to those persons. Thereafter, some other persons withdrew the money of compensation. It has been argued by Mr Afric that the said compensation was not actually paid to the owners of the land in question. If any such grievance is there the aggrieved person may take legal step in Civil Court in a competent suit. In this writ jurisdiction it is difficult for us to consider the submission as made by Mr Afric. 

 27. It further appears from certificate of possession that Requiring Body (page 97), that is, the Housing and Settlement Department, took over possession of some land of .questioned plots namely Plot Nos. 14, 17,27, 33, 57, 62, 63, 65, 66, 65, 68, 73,75, 77, 79, 85, 87, 95, 97 and 117 from Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka, on 28-11-1973. It also transpires from the certificate of possession' (Page 103) that the Requiring Body took over possession of the entire lands of questioned plot Nos. 15, 29, 35,36,41,43,59,61,69,71,76,77,93,94,98,99 and 100 and part of questioned plot Nos. 14, 57, 63, 65; 67, 73, 77, 79,84,88 and 117 of Mouza Chakuli from the Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka. 

 28. The learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners emphatically argued that no notice under section 1 I think it will be 5(1a) has been served upon the petitioners or their predecessors-in-interest but it appears from page 125 to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition that the notices under the provision of section 1 I think it will be 5(1a) of the Act, which is a public notice to be given at the convenient places or near the property proposed to be acquired, were served. It appears that the notices under section 1 I think it will be 5(1 a) of the Act in respect of entire land of questioned plot Nos. 15, 29, 32, 35, 36, 41, 43, 59, 61, 66, 69, 71, 76, 93, 94, 98, 99, 100 and part of questioned plot Nos. 14, 57, 63, 65, 66, 67, 73, 77, 79, 84 and 117 of Chakuli Mouza had been issued to serve by hanging in the Notice Boards of the office of Chairman, Hari Rampur Union Council, Mirpur, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the Police Station, Mirpur, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the Sub-Registrar, Kalabagan, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the LA Collector, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the DC, Dhaka, Notice Board of office of the District Judge, Dhaka, Notice Board of the office of the Commissioner Dhaka Division, Dhaka, Notice Board of the Municipality, Dhaka, and the Notice Board of the Revenue Circle Officer, Mirpur, Dhaka. In such view of the matter it is difficult to accept the sub- mission of the learned Advocates for the petitioners that the notice under section II think it will be 5(1 a) had not been served in accordance 'with law. From the order dated 28-11-1988 it appears that some papers relating requisition and acquisition of land in LA Case No. 5 of 1972-73 were called for by the Anti-Corruption Officer and those papers were found to be untraced. 

 29. In the case of Bangladesh vs Fazle Karim reported in 42 DLR (AD) 91, it has been observed by their Lordships of the Appellate Division that the presumption of service of public notice for acquisition of property being an official act, a presumption is available under the Evidence Act that it has been regularly performed unless the country is proved. Section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, provided that the Court may presume that the judicial and official acts have been regularly performed. Where once making to an order under a statute has been proved, there may well be presumption that it was duly made as required by law. Once the publications of the orders in the official Gazette are established the process of publications should be presumed to have been considered sufficient. Since the proceedings took place long ago the same must be presumed to be regular. Similarly, where the report states that symbolical possession is delivered, there is a presumption as to formalities having been complied with. Irregularity is not to be presumed, but a party alleging it may prove it. The writ petitioners did not take any step to rebut the presumption. 

 “She further submits that according to the plaintiff the properties appertain to the waft estate while the Government claims that it does not from part of the waif estate so, it is a disputed question of fact, which can only be resolved by a civil Court of competent jurisdiction and that suit at the instance of the writ petitioner is still pending and, as such, Rule should be discharged on that account. She further submits that there is no legal bar for fresh requisition for a public purpose of any property which was previously derequisitioned and that notices under section 5(7) having been published as evidence from Annexures-B-B(l) to the writ petition as well as by Annexures 1, 2 and 3 respectively to the affidavit-in-opposition the land in question has absolutely vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and that full compensation has been paid to the normal owners and accordingly, there is no scope for withdrawing from the requisition inasmuch as section 8(B) of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 provides that the Government may withdraw from the process of requisition before compensation is paid and has relief on the case of Abdul Mannan vs Ministry of Land Administration 27 DLR 297 and then their Lordships have observed, 

 "It appears that the High Court Division, considered the plea as to the question of wagestate and the High Court Division answered the question as under (quoted above) 

 33. That is their Lordships did not find any illegality in finding of the High Court Division that there is no legal bar for fresh requisition for a public purpose of any property which was previously derequisitioned. Since the aforesaid Judgment delivered by their Lordships of the Appellate Division regarding the act of acquisition of the land in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 the same is binding upon this Division. 

 34. Here, in the instant petitions it appears to us that some portions of the land were acquired and decision of acquisition was published in the official Gazette on 15-10-1970 under section 5(7) of the Act. The title and possession of those lands were vested in the Government who delivered possessions to the requiring body. Those lands were again requisitioned in LA Case No.5 of 1972-75 and after service of necessary notices and payment of compensation to the said requiring body those lands were again acquired. Some portions of the questioned land were earlier requisitioned but not acquired at the time. Those land were derequisitioned from the proceeding of LA Case No. 90 of 1965-66. Those were again requisitioned and finally acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73. Rest of the lands were requisitioned and thereafter acquired in LA Case No.5 of 1972-73 afresh. After publication of notices in the official Gazette under Section 5(7) of the Act the title and possession of those lands have been vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. Challenge of the notifications as to acquisition of the lands in question published in the Official Gazette on 15-10-1975, 24-11-1988,20-8-1989, 4-9-1990, 28-11-1980 after long lapse of time on the plea of non-services of notices does not deserve any consideration in this summary proceeding. Whether the petitioners had received notices of requisition and acquisition or not is essentially a disputed question of fact which cannot be resolved in writ petition. 

 35. Mr Afric relied on the case of the province of East Pakistan vs Jogesh Chandra Lodh, 11 DLR SC 11 wherein it has been observed that where the officer concerned did not apply his mind to the question the requisition order is invalid. That petition was filed before acquisition, challenging the order of requisition. Similarly case cited by Mr Afric reported in 15 DLR page 453 (Herama Chandra Battacharjee vs The Secretary, Department of Revenue and others the petitioner challenged order of derequisition The citations have got no manner of application in the present case, In the case of Bangladesh vs Nabab Abdul Malik Jute Mills Ltd. reported in 60 DLR(AD) 7 it has been observed by their Lordships of the Appellate Division that once the property is acquired and Gazette Notification is published under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of the Property Act; the fight, title and ,interest, if any, of the owners are extinguished and preparation of Khatian and payment of rent does not improve the position of the original owner in respect of acquired land.
